correctness.rationale: The Ces_p norm is built from levelwise arithmetic means of absolute values, not an ℓp mean. The proof obtains the exact telescope B_gamma^n f(v)=gamma^n c_k/c_{k+n} sum_descendants f; using disjoint descendant partition gives A_k(B^n f)<=|gamma|^n A_{k+n}(f). A Tonelli expansion of the shifted scalar Cesaro norm with nonnegative increments d_j and strictly decreasing zeta-tail ratios proves the sharp scalar bound and uniqueness of the extremizing level. A common-phase level-n vector attains equality. Stirling/integral tail comparison proves the sharp coefficient; an explicit right inverse proves mixing, periodic density and the hypotheses of the standard Frequent Hypercyclicity Criterion for |gamma|>1. At modulus one positive-density root recurrence or a periodic nonzero coordinate contradicts Cesaro summability. No computation is used to infer an infinite-dimensional conclusion.

value.rationale: The sharp norm of the backward shift on ces_p is not provided even in the inspected 2026 classical-space study (only lower/upper bounds). This work supplies exact norms simultaneously for every power and all p>1, a strict classification of maximizers, and a branching-independent law for every irregular rooted tree under the canonical mass-normalized edge weights. The nontrivial sharp polynomial growth constant explains why a mixing/non-frequently-hypercyclic critical example has large, unbounded operator powers, while the full dynamical transition gives the invariant a clear use. This is a natural quantitative invariant, not an arbitrary isolated parameter.
